newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran blasts Britain over terrorism charges.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts Britain over terrorism charges.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Monday rejected British accusations that Iran sponsored "terrorism" and created instability in the Gulf, saying Britain destabilised the region by creating discord between regional states.

"No other factor but the presence of aliens and discord-creating policies has been effective in creating instability in the Persian Gulf, and this is a policy which is being seriously pursued by the United States and Britain," said the radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
The radio was commenting on critical remarks on Iran by Britain's junior Foreign Office Minister Jeremy Hanley.
Speaking in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, Hanley said Britain wanted Iran to recognise "that countries should not sponsor terrorism and not threaten the stability of...their own region".
The radio said such allegations were being made at a time when some British officials, including Britain's Defence Procurement Minister James Arbuthnot, were visiting Arab states in the region.
"Therefore, bringing up discord-creating views against ties between Iran and its Arab neighbours in the Persian Gulf by the British government is well expected," it said.
Tehran says Western states raise the charges of terrorism to justify their military presence in the region and encourage oil-rich Gulf Arab states to buy more Western arms.
